$comment: #NEW-148 / #NEW-143 D1 (Danny 2026-11-26): THE DEVICE HUB AS THE MCP CLIENT OF TEAM SERVERS (host side; the server side is skills.json, elicitation.json, tasks.json; the hub's own rules are hub.json). ROUTING: a launch no longer writes team MCP servers into the agent CLI's config (claude's --mcp-config, codex's overrides). The launcher MOUNTS each resolved team server on the device's ONE hub (apps/desktop crates/emcp hub.rs) FOR THAT RUN ONLY (a run-scoped mount under the server's config key; another run's mount of the same name never sees it; it goes when the run's grant is revoked), grants the run `write` on every one of them and gives the CLI ONE entry, `entry.name`, loopback HTTP with the run's bearer token behind `entry.tokenEnv`. Credentials never reach the CLI's env or config any more; stdio team servers are spawned by the hub with their env. The device's own servers (exponential, computer, codemode, screen) stay their own entries. TOOL NAMES (`toolNameCases`, the migration note): a team tool is hub.json's `<server>__<tool>` on the `team` entry: claude `mcp__team__<server>__<tool>` (was `mcp__<server>__<tool>`), codex `team` server, tool `<server>__<tool>` (was server `<server>`, tool `<tool>`). Code mode reaches them through the `team` upstream the same way. CLIENT CAPABILITIES (`clientCapabilities`): every request the hub sends an upstream declares elicitation form + url and the tasks and skills extensions; never sampling or roots. MRTR (`mrtr`): a `tools/call` answered `input_required` is fulfilled by the hub and RETRIED with a new id, `inputResponses` and the `requestState` echoed, at most `mrtr.maxRounds` rounds (then the call answers an isError result `copy.tooManyRounds`). Each input request: `elicitation/create` = ONE ACP elicitation into the run's session (form: the requestedSchema as is; url: url + elicitationId), its `_meta` naming the server under elicitation-card.json's `serverMetaKey` (domain-contract), so it reaches THE elicitation card; the hub waits for it at most `mrtr.askWaitMs` (the CLI bounds every MCP call at 120 s, coding argv.rs CLAUDE_MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS, and the hub must answer first), then withdraws the card and the call answers isError `copy.noAnswer`; the person's action is the ElicitResult (`elicitResultCases`: accept + content, decline, cancel; no live session to ask = cancel). `roots/list` = `mrtr.roots`. `sampling/createMessage` is never declared: such a call answers isError `copy.sampling`. The CLI always gets ONE plain blocking result (claude does not declare tasks on tools/call, spike §10). TASKS (`tasks`): a call answered `resultType: task` is DRIVEN BY THE HUB: the task id is persisted on the device (`tasks.storeFile` under the data dir, one record per task: `recordKeys`) BEFORE the first poll; a poller calls `tasks/get` every `pollIntervalMs` the task asks for, clamped to [`tasks.poll.min`, `tasks.poll.max`] (`tasks.poll.default` when absent; `pollCases`); every change of status or statusMessage is ONE TraceItem in the session (id `mcp-task:<server>:<taskId>`, title = `<server>: <statusMessage>` or `<server>: <tool>` without one; status by `traceStatus`); `input_required` = its inputRequests answered like MRTR's and sent with `tasks/update {taskId, inputResponses}`; a terminal status ends the record: completed = its `result` is the call's result, failed = an isError result naming its error message, cancelled = isError `copy.cancelled`. The CLI's call waits at most `tasks.callWaitMs` (under the CLI's 120 s); past it the call answers `copy.stillRunning` (not an error) and the poller goes on, its TraceItem with it. STOP (the session's Stop, or the session ending; never a resume's relaunch, which keeps them) sends `tasks/cancel` for every live task of the run's session and ends their records. RESTART: when a run mounts a server again (a resume), its session's persisted tasks on that server are polled again from where they were. TOKENS (EXP-808, reopened by #NEW-148): an upstream answering HTTP 401 makes the hub ask the launcher for the server's credentials again (tRPC `mcpServers.resolveForLaunch`, which refreshes an expiring OAuth token), reconnect and retry the request ONCE; a second 401 or a failed resolve = isError `copy.signIn`. SKILLS (`skills`): at every launch, for every mounted team server that declares the skills extension, the hub lists `skills/list` with the member's credential; each skill's manifest is checked against the limits of skills.json, every file read with `resources/read` and VERIFIED (`verifyCases`: size first, then the `sha256:` digest; one mismatch drops the whole skill with a launch warning). The skill's DIGEST SET (`digestSetCases`) = `sha256:` + hex SHA-256 of the canonical JSON (keys sorted, no whitespace, UTF-8) of its manifest rows {digest, size, uri} sorted by uri. APPROVAL (`approvalCases`): per team, per server, per skill URI, by a team OWNER, BOUND to the digest set (tRPC `mcpServers.skills` lists a server's skills with their state; `mcpServers.approveSkill {serverId, uri, digestSet}` / `mcpServers.revokeSkill {serverId, uri}`, owners; `resolveForLaunch` returns each server's approvals as `skillApprovals: [{uri, digestSet}]`): `approved` = an approval of this uri with this digest set; `changed` = one with another digest set (the skill changed since: it needs a new approval); `pending` = none. Only an APPROVED skill is written into the session skill dir (team_skills.rs, beside the team skills) under `dirName` (`dirNameCases`: `mcp-<server>-<name>`, past 64 chars cut to 55, trailing `-` trimmed, `-` + the first 8 hex of the SHA-256 of the full name); its SKILL.md frontmatter is REWRITTEN to exactly {name: the dir name, description} (`skillMdCases`): `allowed-tools` and every other key are ignored; the other files are written verbatim. A verified copy is CACHED read-only (files 0444, dirs 0555) under `skills.cacheDir`/<server id>/<digest set hex>/ in the data dir, outside every discovery path (never under a session dir, `.claude` or `.codex`), and reused while the digest set matches.

copy.tooManyRounds: {server} kept asking for input; the call was stopped after {rounds} rounds.
copy.sampling: {server} asked this device to run a model (sampling), which it does not offer.
copy.stillRunning: {server} is still working on this (task {taskId}: {status}). It keeps running and shows in the session; its result does not come back to this call.
copy.signIn: {server}: the sign-in expired and could not be refreshed. Reconnect it in Settings › MCP servers.
copy.noAnswer: {server} asked a question in the session that was not answered in time; once the person answered, call the tool again.
